question.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{2x-2} & =2\cdot {9}^{x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2x-2}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\cdot {9}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
2x-2=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\cdot {9}^{x}).
$$

Next, we use the power and product laws of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-2 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+\operatorname{ln}⁡({9}^{x}) \\ 2x-2 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-2 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) \\ 2x-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) & =2+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ x(2-\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)) & =2+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ x & =\frac{2+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}{2-\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)}\end{aligned}
$$
